metadata.name: IRS CP2501 Notice of Delinquency Response
metadata.description: Respond to IRS CP2501 Notice of Delinquency indicating failure to file or pay required taxes.

extraction.description: Extract structured data from IRS CP2501 notice. Identifies taxpayer, tax year, reason for delinquency (failure to file or pay), amount due, and response deadline.

fields.name: taxpayerName
fields.prompt: Extract the full taxpayer name from the notice header.

fields.name: ssn
fields.prompt: Extract the Social Security Number in XXX-XX-XXXX format.

fields.name: taxYear
fields.prompt: Extract the tax year for which the notice was issued.
fields.notes: May be multiple years if combined notice

fields.name: noticeDate
fields.prompt: Extract the notice issue date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

fields.name: responseDeadline
fields.prompt: Extract or calculate response deadline as 30 days from notice date.

fields.name: delinquencyReason
fields.prompt: Identify whether this is for failure to file (FTF) or failure to pay (FTP). Look for language like 'We have not received your return' or 'Payment is overdue'.

fields.name: amountDue
fields.prompt: Extract the total amount claimed to be due, including taxes, penalties, and interest.

fields.name: interestRate
fields.prompt: Extract the current interest rate being charged, if stated.
fields.notes: Interest accrues daily; current rate important for response

fields.name: serviceCenter
fields.prompt: Extract which IRS Service Center issued this notice.

extraction.notes: CP2501 notices are typically 1-2 pages. Focus on identifying specific reason for delinquency claim and all amounts claimed due.

validation.description: Validate response addresses delinquency claim and provides evidence of compliance or reasonable dispute.

rules.name: deadlineCompliance
rules.message: Response must be submitted by deadline. 30 days from notice date is critical.
rules.example_fail: Notice dated March 10, 2024; response submitted April 15, 2024 (6 days late)
rules.example_pass: Notice dated March 10, 2024; response submitted April 8, 2024 (on time)

rules.name: addressDelinquencyClaim
rules.check: response addresses the specific delinquency reason (FTF or FTP)
rules.message: Must address whether return was filed or payment was made, with evidence.
rules.example_fail: Response generic without addressing specific claim
rules.example_pass: Response explains return was filed on [date] with copy of filing receipt; or payment made on [date] with bank statement proof

rules.name: supportingEvidence
rules.check: response includes documentary evidence (return filing proof or payment receipt)
rules.message: Provide filing receipt, bank statement, check image, or other proof of compliance.
rules.example_fail: Claims return was filed but provides no documentation
rules.example_pass: Attached: IRS filing receipt showing return accepted; bank statement showing payment

rules.name: noAdmissionLiability
rules.message: Do not admit error, delay, or wrongdoing. State facts and provide evidence.
rules.example_fail: We apologize for the late filing...
rules.example_pass: The return was filed on [date] as documented by filing receipt

rules.name: professionalFormat
rules.message: Response must be formal business letter addressed to correct service center.
rules.example_pass: Professional letter to Philadelphia Service Center with date and signature

validation.notes: CP2501 responses must clearly establish that delinquency claim is incorrect or has been resolved.

aiPrompt.system: You are a tax correspondence specialist skilled in responding to IRS delinquency notices. You understand IRS procedures, filing requirements, and payment documentation standards. Your role is to help taxpayers respond with clear, factual evidence that addresses the delinquency claim.
aiPrompt.task: Analyze the CP2501 notice and determine if the taxpayer (1) has filed the required return or (2) has made the required payment. If delinquency claim is incorrect, generate a response with evidence proving compliance. If payment arrangement exists, document it. Generate a professional response letter.
aiPrompt.format: Professional business letter addressed to IRS Service Center
constraints: Do not admit error, delay, or failure
Provide only factual information with supporting evidence
Do not make assumptions about filing or payment history
Include all required identifying information (name, SSN, tax year)

input.evidence: IRS Form 1040 filed electronically on April 15, 2023; IRS transcript shows return processed

examples.output: Regarding the notice of delinquency for tax year 2023: Our tax return was timely filed on April 15, 2023, which is confirmed by the attached IRS filing receipt and transcript showing the return was processed and accepted.

aiPrompt.notes: CP2501 notices often result from IRS system errors or miscommunication. Respond promptly with clear evidence.

responseTemplate.description: Professional response to CP2501 delinquency notice

sections.name: header
sections.template:
[Service Center Address]

RE: Response to CP2501 Notice
Tax Year [Year]
SSN: [XXX-XX-XXXX]
Notice Date: [Date]
sections.guidance: Address to correct service center with all identifying information
sections.example:
Philadelphia Service Center

RE: Response to CP2501 Notice
Tax Year 2023
SSN: 234-56-7890
Notice Date: March 10, 2024

sections.name: introduction
sections.template:
Dear Sir or Madam:

We are writing to respond to your CP2501 Notice of Delinquency dated [Date]. We do not agree with the delinquency claim and provide the following explanation.
sections.guidance: Brief acknowledgment and immediate statement of disagreement with claim
sections.example:
Dear Sir or Madam:

We are writing to respond to your CP2501 Notice of Delinquency dated March 10, 2024. We do not agree with the delinquency claim and provide the following explanation.

sections.name: responseBody
sections.template:
If FTF: Our tax return for [year] was filed on [date]. Attached is the filing receipt confirming acceptance of the return.

If FTP: Our payment for [year] taxes was submitted on [date] in the amount of $amount. Attached is proof of payment (bank statement, check image, or payment confirmation).

If both: Both the return was filed and payment was made on respective dates, as documented in the attached evidence.
sections.guidance: Clearly state what action was taken (file or pay) with specific dates and supporting evidence. Drafting notes (generated, not substituted): If FTF; If FTP; If both; amount; respective dates.
sections.example: Our tax return for 2023 was filed electronically on April 15, 2023. The attached IRS filing receipt and transcript confirm that the return was timely received and processed by the IRS.

sections.name: closure
sections.template: We respectfully request that the delinquency notice be withdrawn based on the evidence provided above.
sections.guidance: Simple closing requesting relief based on evidence
sections.example: We respectfully request that the delinquency notice be withdrawn based on the evidence provided above.

sections.name: signature
sections.guidance: Sign, include SSN, and list all attached evidence
sections.example:
Sincerely,

Jane Marie Johnson
Jane Marie Johnson
SSN: 234-56-7890

Enclosures:
- IRS Filing Receipt
- IRS Account Transcript
- Bank Statement (showing payment)

legalFramework.description: CP2501 responses governed by IRS procedural rules for delinquency notices.
authorities: IRC Section 6213 - Right to dispute examination findings
IRS Publication 556 - Examination of Returns, Appeal Rights, and Claims for Refund
precedents: IRS system errors can result in false delinquency notices
Taxpayer's filing/payment proof supersedes IRS delinquency claim
Electronically filed returns create irrefutable filing evidence
Payment can be proven by bank statement, canceled check, or IRS payment receipt
criticalRules: MUST respond within 30 days of notice date
MUST provide documentary evidence (not just assertion)
MUST address specific delinquency claim (FTF or FTP)
MUST maintain professional tone and format

testCases.description: Test CP2501 response for typical delinquency scenarios

cases.name: cp2501-false-ftf
cases.description: False failure-to-file claim when return was actually filed
cases.inputDocument: CP2501 claiming failure to file for 2023; taxpayer has e-file receipt
cases.expectedResponse: Letter states return was filed with attached IRS receipt and transcript proof
successCriteria: Clearly identifies that return was filed
Provides IRS filing receipt as evidence
Does not admit error or delay

cases.name: cp2501-false-ftp
cases.description: False failure-to-pay claim when payment was made
cases.inputDocument: CP2501 claiming unpaid balance; taxpayer has bank statement showing payment
cases.expectedResponse: Letter documents payment with bank statement and check image attached
successCriteria: Clearly identifies payment was made on specific date

downstream: CP505 - Notice of Intent to Levy

implementation.notes: CP2501 is common for system errors and taxpayer confusion. Must be implemented early. Extraction of delinquency reason (FTF vs FTP) is critical.
knownChallenges: Many false delinquency claims result from IRS system issues
Distinguishing between failure to file vs. failure to pay
Obtaining sufficient evidence when records are old
